http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24839v1.summary: Kaer is a multi-agent framework that protects the orchestrator's replanning step from malicious agent feedback, using abstract failure templates and restricted repair operators; it is evaluated on the new Cintra benchmark against Magentic-One and ControlValve.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24839v1.title: Kaer: Security-Aware Replanning for Multi-Agent Systems

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25855v1.summary: HabitusMem is a trained memory writer that stores a personalized LLM agent's beliefs about a user's evolving preferences, each with evidence, scope, and status, and reports top results on PersonaMem-v2 and VitaBench 2.0.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25855v1.title: HabitusMem: Belief Memory over Evolving User Preferences for LLM Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25898v1.summary: A critical review of clinical LLM reliability that covers hallucination, agentic error cascades, process reward modeling, and neuro-symbolic grounding, and argues that certification should audit reasoning steps as well as accuracy.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25898v1.title: Verifiable Logic in Medical LLMs: A Critical Review of Agentic Clinical Reasoning Optimization and Neuro-Symbolic Grounding

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26275v1.summary: dLoop restructures a pretrained diffusion language model into a looped architecture that reapplies a shared block before token commitment, reporting top or tied-top accuracy on GSM8K, MATH, MBPP and HumanEval.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26275v1.title: dLoop: Looped Diffusion Language Models via Recurrent Latent Refinement

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26358v1.summary: A technical report introducing Beam, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters for coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks, with a 1M-token context window and a large-scale asynchronous RL post-training run.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26358v1.title: Beam Model Technical Report

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26423v1.summary: Seer is an inference-time framework that guides small local deep-research agents by using offline-trained tool-response and value models, raising GAIA accuracy for Qwen3.5-4B and 9B models.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26423v1.title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26531v1.summary: An arXiv paper presents an agentic system where LLM agents and deterministic tools optimize ranking-model features across a fleet under cost and QPS limits, improving normalized entropy by 0.31% on average.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26531v1.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26569v1.summary: Introduces EditSafetyBench, a 5,940-pair image-instruction benchmark, and finds that Gemini, GPT, and Qwen refuse far more unsafe text prompts than unsafe images paired with neutral instructions.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26569v1.title: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26613v1.summary: Presents AgentRoboCritic, a framework that analyzes frontier multimodal agents' robot control at the action level across 12 manipulation benchmarks, and releases a 12,844-action annotated dataset and a fine-tuned open-source critic.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26613v1.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26619v1.summary: TideCache is a serving system for hybrid LLMs on CPU-GPU superchips that reallocates GPU memory among cache types and streams KV prefixes layer by layer, implemented in SGLang and tested on GB300 and GH200.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26619v1.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26624v1.summary: PlayCraft is an automated framework in which a vision-based agent plays a game, reports its experience, and a crafter agent revises the game for mastery, yielding larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes than initial games in most cases.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26624v1.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26776v1.summary: Compares three ways of passing observations from perception agents to a language-model reasoner for flagging violent video, finding flat text matches a single audio-visual model (F1 0.967 vs 0.968) on XD-Violence.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26776v1.title: What Helps Language-Model Agents Review Violent Video? A Controlled Comparison with a Human Evidence Reference

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26966v1.summary: Presents the OPCP runtime, which mediates tool calls for AI agents and records uncertain supplier outcomes; tests use scripted requests and synthetic suppliers, with no language model evaluated.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26966v1.title: Keep the Process, Change the Supplier: Runtime Governance for Tool-Using AI Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26972v1.summary: Introduces TheaterBench, a benchmark of counter-intuitive video scenarios that violate physical laws or common sense, used to test how multimodal video models fail when visual evidence conflicts with their priors.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26972v1.title: When Perception Collides with Priors: Diagnosing Modal Polarization in Video Understanding Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26988v1.summary: Proposes a system that converts letter-of-credit bill of lading and invoice requirements into executable checks run by a deterministic verifier, reporting 82% correct verification on 345 real cases against 54% for a tool-using agent.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26988v1.title: From Letter-of-Credit Requirements to Executable Specifications: Evaluating Verification Accuracy and Completeness

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27068v1.summary: DM-PRM uses a general-purpose yes/no decision model to score each step zero-shot, without step labels or fine-tuning, and adds those scores to policy-gradient advantages, improving GRPO on ALFWorld and WebShop.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27068v1.title: Decision Models Are General-Purpose Process Reward Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27084v1.summary: An arXiv paper audits the training-free kNNGuard prompt guardrail, finding its AUROC falls to about 0.55 on inputs over 1000 tokens, and tests length-routed banks, a long-context embedding model, and strided window pooling as fixes.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27084v1.title: Auditing and Adapting kNNGuard for Long-Context Prompts

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27090v1.summary: Across 50 agent systems, public reports show recovery mechanisms used often but rarely fully successful: of 128 real-use reports, 19 describe full recovery, 54 partial and 45 failed.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27090v1.title: Exercised, Rarely Recovered: What Public Reports Say About Recovery in 50 AI Agent Harnesses and Runtimes

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27092v1.summary: PLoQ is a 4-bit activation quantization method for LLMs that estimates a low-rank basis per prompt during prefill, quantizes those dominant components separately, and restores them in the GEMM without changing the weights.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27092v1.title: PLoQ: A Prompt-Specific Low-Rank Basis for 4-bit Quantization of LLM Activations

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27095v1.summary: epistemic-guard v0.5.2 is an open-source Python library and out-of-process stdio MCP receipt proxy that checks agent prose against tool receipts, gates memory writes by provenance, and runs on CPU without GPU VRAM.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27095v1.title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27106v1.summary: Introduces a benchmark protocol and public artifact for LLM business workflows across six Python implementations, reporting that schema validity and task quality diverge, with PydanticAI, LangGraph, and DSPy scoring highest.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27106v1.title: Schema-Validated LLM Workflows: A Benchmark Protocol and Comparative Evaluation Across Six Python Implementations

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27119v1.summary: CTRL is a system that runs an RL learner and a persistent rollout engine on every GPU under CUDA MPS, reporting 1.11-2.24× the throughput of verl's asynchronous baselines across 24 Qwen3 workload settings.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27119v1.title: CTRL: Concurrent Training and Rollout for LLM Reinforcement Learning via GPU Co-Residency

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27124v1.summary: Proposes a round-trip check for latent world model planning that executes plans each CEM iteration and penalizes action mismatches, raising success on DINO-WM, LeWM and JEPA-WM at 0.2% to 3.1% extra planning time.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27124v1.title: A Plan or an Adversarial Example? A Round-Trip Check for Latent World Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27139v1.summary: Introduces RI-Bench, a benchmark measuring whether senior LLM agents uphold their duties toward subordinate reports across peer review, appellate, and parliamentary settings, finding frequent deference to generic reviews and dropped witness limitations.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27139v1.title: Do Senior Agents Do Their Job? Measuring Role Integrity in How LLM Agents Use Subordinate Material

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27154v1.summary: Measures how repetitive full repository histories are for code model training, finding typical repos hold about 19 copies of their current code and that near-duplicate deduplication across versions cuts this to about two.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27154v1.title: Git History Is a Pangenome: Repetition in Code Training Corpora and What Deduplication Removes, Keeps and Misses

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27155v1.summary: Finds that 4-bit quantization of reward models and LLM judges flips 1.1-12.3% of RewardBench preference decisions even when benchmark accuracy barely changes, and that these flips alter best-of-64 selections far more often than final answers.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27155v1.title: The Vulnerability Window: Decision Instability in Quantized Reward Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27216v1.summary: Reports a failure in which an on-device agent's earlier correct release of an item makes it more likely to wrongly release a still-restricted item, tested across 13 open-weight models, with a LoRA-based fix proposed.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27216v1.title: Correct Precedents Induce Policy Violations in On-Device LLM Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27294v1.summary: HookEvo uses an agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses, reporting 95.41% on ALFWorld and 70.56% on DBBench with a frozen Qwen3-4B executor, and releasing code.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27294v1.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27301v1.summary: Tracks 6,503 clinical cases across six HPO releases (Oct 2021–June 2026) and finds diagnostic rankers' accuracy jumps when a case's source publication enters HPO, then collapses when those links are removed.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27301v1.title: Observed, Curated, Reused: Observation Bias in Clinical AI Evaluation

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27306v1.summary: γ-Scape is a simulation and benchmark platform where agents compose motion tools and learned skills to complete mobile manipulation tasks in a persistent physical world, with tools for task evaluation and demonstration collection.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27306v1.title: $γ$-Scape: An Agent-Centric World for Mobile Embodied Intelligence

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27326v1.summary: The paper proposes concept-normalized multilingual scratchpads and reversible model-adaptive reasoning codes to cut the token count, and so the inference cost, of chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27326v1.title: Reasoning in Fewer Tokens: Concept-Normalized Multilingual Scratchpads and Reversible Model-Adaptive Reasoning Codes

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27344v1.title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27350v1.summary: Introduces GRACE, a 4,028-question GraphRAG benchmark built from LC-QuAD 2.0 queries over Wikidata with four controlled evidence interventions, and proposes QCFSE-SA, which raises controlled-state accuracy from 57.17% to 62.78%.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27350v1.title: GRACE: Controlled Evidence Interventions for Diagnosing and Improving Knowledge Integration in GraphRAG

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27376v1.summary: Proposes CSPD, which freezes the pre-RL model, distills each RL expert into a soft prompt, and composes them by concatenation; it matches multi-teacher distillation (67.83 vs. 67.79) with less serving overhead.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27376v1.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27443v1.summary: Introduces ADAPT, a post-training recipe that teaches a small language model when to request advice from a stronger advisor model, reporting higher success rates on TextWorld, LiveCodeBench and GAIA with about 1 to 2 advisor calls per task.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27443v1.title: Learning When to Ask: Advisor-Aware Post-Training for SLM Agents

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27521v1.title: PaMuk-Bench: A Parallel Multilingual Multitask Benchmark for Vision-Language Tasks

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27536v1.summary: Introduces Open CDLM, a benchmark and open-source library for evaluating continuous diffusion language models, using Kernel Text Discrepancy and diversity diagnostics, and shows that conventional generation scores can be inflated by collapsed outputs.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27536v1.title: Open CDLM: A Benchmark and Library for Continuous Diffusion Language Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27607v1.summary: Introduces Tasklets, a set of small synthetic tasks testing recall, sequence manipulation, and state tracking, and uses them to compare many language model sequence-mixing layer types in controlled small-model experiments.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27607v1.title: Tasklets: A Unit-Test Benchmark for Language Model Architectures

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27652v1.summary: Studies post-training machine unlearning in the diffusion language model LLaDA-8B-Instruct, using WMDP as the forget benchmark and sparse autoencoders to compare static and stage-adaptive feature suppression across denoising steps.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27652v1.title: Auditing Post-Training Unlearning in Diffusion Language Models using Sparse Autoencoders

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27673v1.summary: Hy-MT3 is a third-generation multilingual translation model family in 1.8B, 7B and 30B-A3B sizes, expanding language coverage from 38 to 102 languages.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27673v1.title: Hy-MT3: More Accurate, Robust and Practical Multilingual Translation Models in the Wild

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27721v1.summary: Compares three decision models and two LLMs in zero-shot use against fine-tuned multilingual encoders for four-emotion classification across 10 social-media datasets in five languages.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27721v1.title: Decision Models for Multilingual Emotion Classification: A Comparative Study Against LLMs and Encoders

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27722v1.summary: Evaluates language models on seven scientific argumentation tasks (argument mining, rebuttal generation, discourse reasoning) using research papers, peer reviews, and grant proposals, and proposes a training framework that scaffolds argumentative reasoning.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27722v1.title: Beyond Math, Code, and Logic: Do Reasoning Models Transfer to Scientific Argumentation?

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27734v1.title: AutoOntologyBench: A Task-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Knowledge Engineering

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27741v1.summary: Introduces PlayScriptBench, a benchmark testing whether vision-language models can write executable game-playing programs, evaluated on 16 games across 4 genres, where even strong models perform poorly.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27741v1.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27750v1.summary: Introduces RoSci-Bench, a 1,220-sample diagnostic benchmark testing science vision-language models on information errors and losses, and RoSci-Agent, a Parse-Verify-Decide pipeline that outperforms standalone VLMs on an Overall Robustness Score.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27750v1.title: RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27759v1.title: DPMA: Learning to Compress Mixture-of-Experts Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27780v1.summary: Search-RSI is a self-improvement framework for multimodal search agents that expands the retrieval world with new tasks and evidence, reporting 9.8 and 9.5 point average accuracy gains at 9B and 27B across nine benchmarks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27780v1.title: Search-RSI: Expanding Search Worlds Along Multimodal Agents' Capability Frontier

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27784v1.summary: Neural Defend presents ARCAS 290M, a single frozen detector for AI-generated audio that it reports ranks first on the Podonos leaderboard and beats commercial and published detectors on ten public benchmarks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27784v1.title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27811v1.summary: Proposes shallow neural networks alternating simple-cell-like and complex-cell-like layers that give low confidence on unknown and adversarial inputs and remain competitive on standard classification benchmarks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27811v1.title: Redesigning Neural Networks to Not be Confidently Wrong even to Strong Adversarial Attacks

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27823v1.summary: Proposes MoLR, an adaptive recursion method for LoRA that recursively refines each token's down-projected latent with a shared transformation, using a threshold router to set depth, and reports gains over LoRA variants with negligible extra parameters.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27823v1.title: Mixture of Latent Recursions for Low-Rank Adaptation

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27839v1.summary: Introduces a multi-agent framework for verifying research claims that uses asymmetric Advocate, Skeptic and Arbitrator roles and a Belief-Delta stopping rule, reporting 2.4x fewer LLM calls across 200 runs on 40 hypotheses with DeepSeek-R1-32B.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27839v1.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27865v1.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27899v1.summary: Describes a two-tier industrial framework for automated UX attribution in web search: a fine-tuned Gemini XS telemetry model for macro sentiment regression detection, and a Gemini 3.0 Pro multimodal model for layout-level diagnostics.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27899v1.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27910v1.summary: Proposes interpretable embeddings built from yes/no/not-stated answers to natural-language questions, reporting that they match dense retrieval for entity matching on public product benchmarks while giving exact per-question explanations.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27910v1.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27915v1.summary: Introduces StereoVLM, a binocular vision-language model trained hierarchically on calibrated stereo images, reporting 95.17% depth accuracy and a 66.98 object-level score on its new Stereo3D-Bench.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27915v1.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27919v1.summary: The paper proposes Spectral Universal Advantage Features (SUAF), reward-independent representations derived from an action-centered canonical dependence matrix, and reports finite-state and zero-shot evaluations on discrete and continuous-control tasks.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27919v1.title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27951v1.summary: Introduces Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT), a linear-size attention method using sparsemax or thresholded ReLU gating, annealed Sinkhorn scaling and custom Triton kernels, reporting 97.40% zero-shot recall at L=262,144 on an NVIDIA L4.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27951v1.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27962v1.summary: Introduces Model Carving, which uses learnable scalar gates on each sublayer to learn Transformer weights and architecture together in one run, reporting lower validation loss than dense models at equal compute.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27962v1.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27963v1.summary: Introduces NoPeBench and NoPeWorld, which trains a small head on frozen diffusion transformer hidden states to flag and replace penetrating actions, cutting the average violation rate across six models from 74% to 16%.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27963v1.title: Non-penetrating World Models

http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27973v1.summary: MemOnce proposes an LLM architecture that caches compact final-layer hidden states as memory and decodes them into KV caches, reporting a 1313× smaller memory state cache and 6.9× lower prefill latency for Qwen3.5-4B at 1M context.
http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27973v1.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models

https://agentclock.andalabx.com.summary: AgentClock is a public MCP server offering AI agents a time tool, clock_now, which returns the current UTC and Unix time with optional timezone rendering, plus a clock_status tool for source and sync details.
https://agentclock.andalabx.com.title: Show HN: I built an MCP server that gives AI agents a reliable clock

https://agentmemories.ai.summary: An open evaluation platform benchmarks textual, coding, and multimodal agent memory systems using participant-hosted Add/Search APIs, with a full-evaluation submission deadline of November 4, 2026 at 23:59 (UTC+8).
https://agentmemories.ai.title: How do you shortlist an agent memory system?

https://amund.blog/modded-nanogpt-sub-30.summary: A third Track 1 modded-nanogpt speedrun attempt, stacked on PR #404, reports 29.90 seconds across 12 runs on one rented 8×H100 node, versus 30.05 seconds for #404 on the same node; it is under review as PRs #406 and #407.
https://amund.blog/modded-nanogpt-sub-30.title: Sub-30s LLM Pretraining on 8×H100? Modded-NanoGPT World Record Attempt (29.90 S)

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-lea.summary: An AWS ML blog post describes a distributed KV caching skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS that uses Amazon ElastiCache to cut self-hosted LLM inference cost by up to 40% and time to first token by up to 80%.
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-lea.title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-lea.summary: An AWS Machine Learning Blog post announces a SageMaker HyperPod feature that routes inference requests through one endpoint spanning multiple AWS Regions and clusters.
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-lea.title: Introducing Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Global Inference Gateway: One endpoint across Regions and clusters

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-lea.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod adds managed cluster extensions for observability and user management on Slurm clusters, configurable through declarative, API, and console methods, and the post follows a platform team running one for a quarter.
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-lea.title: Introducing managed cluster extensions for observability and user management in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Slurm

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-lea.summary: AWS Quick releases updates including chat-built business-process flows, an updated web app, multi-agent answers, and new data connectors for Meta ads and Amplitude.
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-lea.title: New in AWS Quick: More capable flows, an updated web experience, and agents that work together

https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/te.summary: Gemini API's Tool Retrieval, now in preview in the Interactions API, loads tool parameter schemas on demand via a tool_search tool and defer_loading flag to cut input tokens and latency.
https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/te.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API

https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/microsoft-.summary: NVIDIA and Microsoft announced at Microsoft Ignite expanded access to Azure virtual machines with NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, now running in Azure data centers, plus new edge and Windows PC options.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/microsoft-.title: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs

https://chittios.com.summary: ChittiOS is a bare-metal operating system written in Rust, without POSIX, libc or ELF, that runs a small language model on the hardware and gates the model's actions through capability and taint checks.
https://chittios.com.title: ChittiOS – an OS where the agent is the driver

https://chszlab.github.io/AgenticAlgorit.title: Show HN: An agent skill that optimizes code with falsifiable hypotheses

https://claude.dev/blog/chaos-loop-claud.summary: Anthropic describes how it used a long-running Claude Code loop, with sub-agents, to stress-test a staging cluster before the September 16, 2026 launch of Claude Docs, reporting 60 server errors across 2 billion requests.
https://claude.dev/blog/chaos-loop-claud.title: Using a "chaos loop" to harden the Claude Docs launch: 60 server errors across billions of requests

https://claude.dev/blog/how-the-claude-c.summary: Explains how end-to-end, property and differential tests let coding agents verify their work, and how the Claude Code team keeps its verifiers reliable, noting that about 90% of its code is written and reviewed by Claude.
https://claude.dev/blog/how-the-claude-c.title: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification

https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/d.summary: AlloyDB Omni, Google's downloadable PostgreSQL-compatible database, can now connect to locally hosted models such as Gemma 4 and Qwen3.8, which SQL queries can call so data stays on-premises.
https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/d.title: Data + AI Anywhere: AlloyDB Omni integration with local models

https://deepmind.google/blog/genie-4-is-.summary: Google DeepMind is rolling out Genie 4 and a new Project Genie experience to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, with real-time prompt editing, native audio, and a community gallery; Pro members can join a waitlist.
https://deepmind.google/blog/genie-4-is-.title: Genie 4 is now available

https://eugeneyan.com/writing/public-eva.summary: Eugene Yan's essay examines how public AI model evals work and fail, reporting that a grader wrongly failed passing work in eight of twelve evals studied, and covers grading and scoring design choices.
https://eugeneyan.com/writing/public-eva.title: How Public Evals Work and Fail, and What Should Change

https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode.summary: Jcode is an open-source coding agent harness that runs multiple agents in parallel on the same repo, with a server that notifies agents of file changes and manages messaging and swarm coordination.
https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode.title: Jcode: High performance coding agent harness written in Rust

https://github.com/alicexixi85/geo-seo-m.summary: An MIT-licensed, open-source MCP server that runs five deterministic checks on a public website's readiness for AI search crawlers and classic search, returning a prioritized FAIL/WARN fix list without API keys or an account.
https://github.com/alicexixi85/geo-seo-m.title: Show HN: Open-source MCP server to check AI search crawler readiness

https://github.com/ameesme/shoebox.summary: shoebox is a tool where each AI agent is a folder with its own Docker image, and a main agent delegates Markdown-file tasks to them, starting containers automatically and reporting back when tasks finish or get blocked.
https://github.com/ameesme/shoebox.title: Show HN: Crazy simple AI agent orchestration with Markdown and Containers
